overall_summary: After deduplicating 36 unique Shorts, performance shows a sharp polarization: immersive, visceral 'What If You Fell Into...' and extreme cosmic survival scenarios (e.g., liquid diamond, burning ice, coal-dark exoplanets) consistently hit channel peaks (800–1,050+ views and 20–38 likes). In contrast, generic psychology snippets ('fake memories', 'songs stuck in head') and repeated re-uploads of identical scripts consistently languish under 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-person hazard & 'What If You Fell Into...' hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,030 views, 36 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) dominate view velocity and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on sensory-rich, first-person survival scenarios involving extreme alien environments and planetary physics.

winning_patterns.pattern: Counterintuitive physical anomalies with superlative framing
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views, 25 likes) demonstrate strong organic retention compared to mundane science facts.
winning_patterns.action: Pair bizarre astrophysical real-world mechanics with vivid, cinematic sensory descriptions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5, 10, 53 views) and 'Songs Stuck In Your Head' (17, 71 views) generated virtually zero viewer interaction.
weak_patterns.action: Pause dry psychology facts; pivot human/biological content toward high-stakes survival biology or extreme evolutionary adaptations.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeatedly publishing identical concepts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' and 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' shows diminishing and erratic distribution across attempts.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict deduplication; prioritize 100% fresh, unexplored celestial and geographical subjects.
